claims.text: Stainless steel with its native surface is vulnerable to extreme corrosion in challenging environments.
Conventional duplex stainless steel exhibits substantial corrosion in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 at elevated temperatures.
Untreated stainless steel performance can be insufficient in high-temperature molten-salt environments.
Atomic layer deposition can produce a conformal, nanometer-scale oxide coating on stainless steel.
An ALD oxide coating on stainless steel will significantly improve corrosion resistance under extreme aggressive conditions.
ALD provides precise control over the thickness and composition of an ultrathin oxide layer.
The ultrathin oxide layer acts as a protective diffusion barrier.
The ALD-deposited oxide physically and chemically limits diffusion of corrosive species.
In situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy enables real-time monitoring of coating barrier properties and integrity under extreme conditions.
ALD-coated stainless steel will have a lower corrosion rate than uncoated stainless steel under the same aggressive exposure.
ALD-coated stainless steel will exhibit improved surface impedance relative to uncoated stainless steel.
The corrosion-resistance benefit depends on the ultrathin coating remaining intact.
Delamination or coating degradation during prolonged exposure or mechanical stress may limit the corrosion-resistance benefit.
The magnitude of corrosion improvement depends on oxide composition, thickness, and adhesion quality.
Optimization of the oxide layer is required to ensure long-term integrity in extreme environments.
